ruling: - **R28. Every prose store is tended one shared way.** Owner 10:19 CST Nov 11: "everything that marks prose should share the same "tending" mechanism ... it should be more uniform, standardized, and shared as much as possible to avoid stale duplication and to ensure shared best practrices". Stores: decisions, rules, docs and README, debts, handoffs, the feedback log, the roadmap and queue. Owner 11:39 CST Nov 11 adds the git copies of each repo's page and the mailbox: "i agree the fix is in r28". Case: claude-settings' copy fell about 11 h behind its live page (read 11:30 CST); the copy step and the Stop check both missed (triage, 11:39 CST). A copy's "still true?" test compares it with its live source. Step waiting-export-miss-cloud fixes the check. Audit 11:40 CST: degen, home and mailaudit copies 35-40 h old, banchi 5 days; q_max, joyous and ios-adblock have no copy. Owner 11:45 CST: "is the live page being used correctly then if the data in there needs to be manually copied in and out? i figured it's just temporally same as with git? it feels weird that it's partitioned steps". Decision waiting-data-in-repo rules git the home and the page a view, but today sessions and the owner write the page first and git copies it later. The design pass makes git the first write, and names how an owner answer reaches git with no session awake. Owner 11:50 CST: "ya if anything the actual page gets its database disableed if that's possible and then it's never an issue ... remember ij just care about the outcomes not the plumbing to reach it". The outcome: one store, no copy step, no lag; the design pass picks the route. Read 11:52 CST: a page can call the viewer's claude.ai connectors (capability mcp), the built-in Claude Code Remote one included. So an answer can wake its writer today. This account has no GitHub connector, so a page cannot write git directly yet. The other account is unread. Owner 11:55 CST: "The fallback is moving off artifacts to your own site ... this doesnt sound so bad tho tbh" and "maybe a PAT or a github API resolves this and we just go via that?". A token must never sit in a page: every viewer can read the page and its data. So a token route is a small server that holds it, such as a Cloudflare Worker that writes git through the GitHub API. That is the own-site route, now a full option beside the other two. Box answer before 10:22 CST: "i think a skim audit just for some overarching context and to avoid common pitfalls is best .. thetn shared/log-fix, then a deeper audit". Order: 1. A read-only skim audit of how each store is tended now (started before 10:22 CST). 2. A design pass sets one shared contract in lint/layout.json: per store, the item shape, a "still true?" test, and a close step. One runner calls it from points that already run: the merge check, the Stop hooks, compaction and triage status. No new timer or process. R27 is its first user. 3. A deeper audit, then each other store moves over when a lane next touches it. Home: a new decision for the shared contract; R27's step waits on step 2. PARTLY SUPERSEDED (retro audit of #2829, 12:01 CST Nov 13; filed by triage): page item 593 a (owner 12:40 CST Nov 12) makes the database the store and git a timely backup. The outcome stays: one store, no lag. The gap the audit found, cross-account reads of the git copy (owner 11:34 CST Nov 11), goes into #2829's fixes.
